verifiedFacts.claim: server_tool_use blocks are executed by the API; unlike client tool_use, no tool_result is needed; ids use srvtoolu_ prefix
Client and server tools can be combined in the same request / parallel tool group
'Can you suggest some changes' leads Claude to suggest rather than implement; a system prompt such as 'By default, implement changes rather than only suggesting them' makes it act
Docs do not attribute this behavior to temperature or tool descriptions
--system-prompt replaces the entire default prompt; --system-prompt-file also replaces
--append-system-prompt appends to the default prompt and preserves default tool guidance; recommended when Claude should remain a coding assistant with extra rules
--bare skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, CLAUDE.md etc.; it does not restore the default prompt
Python SDK list methods auto-paginate when iterated: for batch in client.messages.batches.list(limit=20) fetches more pages as needed; .data holds only the current page
PreToolUse hook can return hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput with permissionDecision 'allow' to auto-approve a rewritten file_path (sandbox redirect example)
Docs: always return a new object rather than mutating the original tool_input; returning {} allows without changes
max_budget_usd / maxBudgetUsd stops the query when the client-side cost estimate reaches the USD value
ResultMessage subtypes include success, error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd, error_during_execution; ResultMessage carries session_id; result is optional
A single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result

issues: Minor: mixes TypeScript option name (maxBudgetUsd) with the Python type name (ResultMessage; TS type is SDKResultMessage). Not answer-affecting.
suggestedFix: Optionally use 'max_budget_usd' with ResultMessage (Python) or 'maxBudgetUsd' with the result message (TypeScript) consistently across options.

verifiedFacts.claim: With tool_choice any or tool, the API prefills the assistant turn and the model will not emit natural-language explanation before tool_use, even if asked
Docs recommendation for explanation plus a specific tool: use tool_choice auto with explicit instructions in the user message

issues: Two defensible answers: B is the documented recommendation (auto + instruction), but the stem's hard requirement 'every request must produce a ticket' is only guaranteed by keeping the forced tool_choice, which favors D (reason field in the schema also satisfies the audit-log need).
Under B the ticket guarantee becomes instruction-based; under D the explanation is in tool input rather than a text block 'before filing'. The stem does not say which constraint dominates.
suggestedFix: Decide the key and remove the competing path. If key=D: state explicitly that the team must keep a guaranteed file_ticket call on every request (and drop 'before filing'). If key=B: remove 'every request must produce a ticket' (e.g., 'nearly every request should produce a ticket and a reviewer checks misses') and replace D with a clearly non-viable distractor (e.g., add the explanation request to the tool description).

verifiedFacts.claim: Rules in .claude/rules/ with paths frontmatter load only when Claude reads/writes/edits matching files; glob patterns like src/**/* supported
@imports are expanded and loaded at launch and do not reduce context cost
Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files load on demand; CLAUDE.local.md is personal, not shared
HTTP 413 request_too_large: request exceeds max bytes; Messages API max request size 32 MB
For large PDFs, upload with the Files API and reference by file_id to keep payloads small; PDF pages are converted to images (scanned content readable)
Read deny rules apply to built-in file tools and to file commands Claude Code recognizes in Bash (cat, head, tail, sed, tee) and redirections; not to arbitrary subprocesses
Managed settings permission rules cannot be overridden by any other level
.claudeignore has no effect; use Read deny rules
Managed policy CLAUDE.md cannot be excluded by individual settings; recommended for data handling and compliance reminders; settings for technical enforcement
MCP tool execution errors (API failures, business logic errors) are reported in the result with isError: true so the model can act on them

issues: Note: error category / retryable fields are an application convention, not MCP-spec fields; option wording ('error content giving...') is compatible with that.

verifiedFacts.claim: Clear, explicit criteria and few-shot examples improve accuracy and consistency
Being specific about desired output and constraints improves results; vague instructions are less effective
Structured outputs support string format 'date' (and date-time etc.) and simple regex patterns; JSON outputs and strict tool use share the same limitations
Constrained decoding guarantees schema compliance, not semantic correctness of values
Subagents should return work with clear output formats/boundaries; coordinator must preserve information rather than lose it in handoffs
Restarts from the beginning are costly; resume from where the agent was when errors occurred; store plans/work in external memory/systems and pass references
